clue.text: Words not delivered as intended could cause spoonerism on being expressed

parts.note: a pledge not delivered as intended has been broken; these words do double duty with the definition

indicators.note: could cause says the remaining letters, once rearranged, produce the second word, with the first word of the answer itself being the signal that they are shuffled
expressed means squeezed out, so the little word just before it is pressed out of the word spoonerism

explanation.surface: A remark about slips of the tongue: words that come out wrongly when someone speaks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spoonerism' tempts a solver to swap sounds, but no swap happens. With ON pressed out, SPERISM is left; the answer's first word, BROKEN, is the anagram signal that turns those letters into its second word.
explanation.definitionFit: Pledges not honoured are words that were not delivered in the way the speaker said they would be.

clue.text: I'm replacing fish in country — a problem for some consumers?

indicators.note: I'm replacing fish means the letters of I'm take the place of the fish inside the country

parts.note: Bulgaria is a country in the Balkans
a gar is a long-snouted fish
taken as its letters, I and M

explanation.surface: Someone muses on a fish shortage abroad and how it affects shoppers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Consumers' suggests shoppers, but here it means eaters: the question mark flags the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: This eating disorder is a problem for some people who eat, which is what consumers means here.

clue.text: Ancient city supports no capacity to exist

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece that supports others sits below them

parts.note: O is a zero, nothing, so it stands for no
cc, cubic capacity, measures an engine's capacity
Ur was an ancient city of Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: An archaeologist notes that an ancient city keeps up its claim to have no room to exist.
explanation.definitionFit: To be found or to happen somewhere is to be present there, so the two verbs overlap.

clue.text: Northern Ireland and Belfast maybe underwrite the cycling race

indicators.note: in a down clue, pieces that write themselves underneath go below what comes first
cycling sends the first letter of the word the round to the end

parts.note: Belfast is an example of a city

explanation.surface: Northern Ireland and Belfast sponsor a bicycle race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cycling race' looks like a bike event, but 'cycling' acts on 'the', making ETH, and 'race' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Race and this word both mean a group sharing descent or cultural identity.

clue.text: See 1
US politician unwrapped free gift; former president's wife's upset

indicators.note: unwrapped means the outer letters of the word free are taken off

parts.note: a present is a gift

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: Evita was the popular name of Eva Perón, wife of the Argentine president Juan Perón

explanation.surface: A tale of political gift-giving gone wrong: a congressman's free present leaves an ex-first lady upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unwrapped' and 'gift' share a scene but do separate jobs: 'unwrapped' strips FREE to RE. 'Upset' reverses EVITA to ATIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the US House is formally called a congressional representative.

clue.text: Marriage witness's cap is upside down!

indicators.note: the cap of a down entry is its top letter, and a W turned upside down looks like an M

parts.note: to witness is to watch

explanation.surface: An excited remark at a wedding: the witness's hat has been put on the wrong way up.
explanation.walkthrough: The change is visual: W inverted on the page becomes M.
explanation.definitionFit: A marriage is a union of two people, and a good pairing is called a match.

clue.text: Search for aliens around weirdly green wildlife area

indicators.note: around means the search programme's letters go round the others

parts.note: SETI is the Search for Extraterrestrial Intelligence

indicators.note: weirdly signals that the letters of green are rearranged

explanation.surface: Alien-hunters scour a strangely green nature reserve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Weirdly' is the anagram signal for the colour word, and 'around' says the alien-search acronym encloses the result.
explanation.definitionFit: This Tanzanian national park is famous for its migrating herds, a classic wildlife area.

clue.text: Corrupt payment to half of upright characters

parts.note: a sub is a subscription, a regular payment

indicators.note: half of means only the first four of the eight letters are kept

parts.note: vertical means upright

explanation.surface: A bribe is paid to some honest people to bend them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upright characters' suggests honest people; here 'upright' is VERTICAL and half of its letters are used.
explanation.definitionFit: To corrupt someone is to undermine their loyalty or principles, a verb sense of the answer.

clue.text: Militant's radio broadcast reveals old-fashioned values

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered, so the letters of the two words are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A militant group's radio station puts out conservative views.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' fits radio perfectly but is the anagram signal for MILITANTSRADIO.
explanation.definitionFit: Clinging to customs and beliefs of the past is a commitment to old-fashioned values.

clue.text: One of those across the top goes forward hard then straight back

definitions.text: One of those across the top

parts.note: in rugby a lock is a forward in the second row
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

indicators.note: back means the word for straight is read backwards

parts.note: pure means straight, undiluted

explanation.surface: A rugby player charges forward hard, then goes straight back.
explanation.walkthrough: The top row of the grid holds three Trump campaign slogans; this is one.
explanation.definitionFit: This chant about Hillary Clinton was a Trump rally slogan, one of the phrases printed in the top row.

clue.text: Both robot's shoulders vibrate

indicators.note: the words carry the answer on their shoulders, holding it inside them

explanation.surface: A robot's two shoulders shake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shoulders' looks like the robot's body parts but is a verb: the words carry the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To beat or pulse rhythmically is to vibrate, as a headache or an engine does.

clue.text: Deflected opening shot following kick-off to Manchester United

indicators.note: following means the second piece comes after the first
the kick-off to a word is its first letter
shot means destroyed, so the opening letter is lost

parts.note: parried means deflected, as a blow or a shot

explanation.surface: A football report: a shot is deflected early in a Manchester United match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Manchester United' looks like one name; 'United' is the definition and only M comes from Manchester.
explanation.definitionFit: A married couple are joined in wedlock, so they are united.

clue.text: To improve matters soldiers risk deposing leaders

indicators.note: deposing leaders means the first letter of each word is removed

parts.note: men are soldiers, as opposed to officers
to chance something is to risk it

explanation.surface: Military advice: to make things better, the troops should risk overthrowing their commanders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deposing leaders' removes the M of MEN and the C of CHANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: To make something better in quality or value is to improve it.

clue.text: Excuse me leaving meal before I begin its starters

indicators.note: leaving means the word me goes out of the word meal
the starters of two words are their first letters

explanation.surface: Someone asks to be excused from dinner before its first courses arrive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starters' plays on the meal's first course; here it means first letters, B and I.
explanation.definitionFit: A claim of being elsewhere when a crime happened is an excuse that clears a suspect.

clue.text: Hint at batting with declaration of 22/8

parts.note: in cricket, the side batting is in

indicators.note: a declaration is something said aloud, so the words are pronounced

parts.note: 22 refers to the answer at 22 Down, a word for strength, and 8 is eight

explanation.surface: A cricket score: a team batting declares at 22 for 8.
explanation.walkthrough: 22/8 reads like a cricket score, but 22 is the answer to 22 Down, SINEW, and saying SINEW EIGHT gives SINUATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To suggest something indirectly is to hint at it.

clue.text: Maintenance work on hole in the wall in shelter

indicators.note: in means these letters go inside the shelter

parts.note: a tent is a shelter
re means on, concerning
hole in the wall is British slang for a cash machine, an ATM

explanation.surface: Repairs to a hole in the wall of a shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hole in the wall' looks like damage needing repair but is a cash machine.
explanation.definitionFit: Care given to keep something in good order, such as a wood finish, is a kind of maintenance work.

clue.text: Suddenly arrived during nosh-up with appropriate drink

indicators.note: during means the arrival is put inside the meal word
in a down clue, up means the word for nosh is read bottom to top

parts.note: to nosh is to eat
someone who blew in arrived suddenly

explanation.surface: A guest arrives unannounced in the middle of a feast, bringing a fitting wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nosh-up' looks like a feast; 'up' reverses EAT to TAE.
explanation.definitionFit: Everyday wine served with a meal is the drink appropriate for the dinner table.

clue.text: Reason for chiropodist's attentions to be tentative

definitions.meaning: read literally, a foot full of pus would send someone to a foot doctor
to tread warily and avoid committing oneself

explanation.walkthrough: The first definition splits the word as a pus-filled foot.
explanation.definitionFit: To act cautiously and avoid commitment is to be tentative; literally, an infected foot needs a chiropodist.

clue.text: Place German vehicle on top of Triumph Acclaim

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means the car sits above the next piece

parts.note: Pl. is the abbreviation for place in addresses
Audi is a German car maker

indicators.note: the top of a down word is its first letter

explanation.surface: An Audi is placed on a Triumph, to the applause of onlookers.
explanation.walkthrough: Triumph is a British car marque, which makes it look like a second vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: Praise or applause given to someone is acclaim.

clue.text: One of those across the top had blue twill pants

definitions.text: One of those across the top

indicators.note: pants is British slang for rubbish, so the letters are a mess and need rearranging

explanation.surface: A description of someone's blue twill trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pants' looks like trousers but is British slang for rubbish, the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Trump's pledge of a barrier on the Mexican border was one of the campaign slogans in the top row.

clue.text: Judge filling in legal document is mistaken

indicators.note: filling in means the judge goes inside the document

parts.note: a deed is a legal document
lud, as in m'lud, is how a judge is addressed in court

explanation.surface: A judge filling in a legal form gets it wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Filling in' suggests completing a form, but here it means one word goes inside another. M'lud is how British barristers address a judge.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone holding false beliefs is wrong in their thinking, that is mistaken.

clue.text: There's nothing odd in warmonger's viral illness

indicators.note: keeping nothing of the odd letters leaves only the even ones

explanation.surface: A warmonger's strange viral disease leaves nothing unusual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nothing odd in' means keep only the even letters: AMNES from warmonger's and IA from viral.
explanation.definitionFit: Loss of memory is a medical condition, a kind of illness.

clue.text: Strength of card players holding one over their opponents

indicators.note: in a down clue, over puts one piece above the next
holding means the partners go round the next piece

parts.note: in bridge, North and South play as partners
I is the Roman numeral one
in bridge, East and West oppose North and South

explanation.surface: Bridge players with one ace have the upper hand over their opponents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Card players' are the bridge partners North and South; their opponents are East and West.
explanation.definitionFit: Tendon tissue stands for physical power, as in strength of mind and sinew.

clue.text: See 19
Expression of woe about temperature range

indicators.note: about means the cry goes round the next piece

parts.note: alas is a cry of grief

explanation.surface: Someone sighs at how wide the range of temperatures is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Range' looks like a span of figures; it is a mountain range in North Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: The Atlas Mountains of Morocco and Algeria form a mountain range.

clue.text: In wet, wet weather, wet and extremely hazardous moving one of those across the top

definitions.text: one of those across the top

indicators.note: In at the front means the other pieces go inside the first word for wet

parts.note: damp means wet
rain is wet weather

indicators.note: moving means the letters shift into a new order
extremely means the outermost letters of hazardous

explanation.surface: A dangerous journey through relentless rain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wet' appears three times with three jobs: a synonym that holds everything, part of a phrase for rainfall, and anagram fodder for 'moving'. The top row of the grid holds Trump slogans.
explanation.definitionFit: Trump's promise to purge Washington of insiders was one of the slogans in the top row.

clue.text: Persuaded home under cover around middle of night

parts.note: in means at home

indicators.note: around means the covered word goes round the next piece

parts.note: veiled means covered, hidden

indicators.note: the middle of a word is its central letter

explanation.surface: Someone is coaxed home in the middle of the night under cover of darkness.
explanation.definitionFit: To coax someone by flattery or deception is to persuade them.

clue.text: See 25
Let all the viola players fiddle behind their backs

indicators.note: the backs of the words are their last letters

explanation.surface: All the viola players play behind the conductor's back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fiddle' suggests a string instrument, but every word up to 'behind' gives its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Property let out on a lease has been rented to a tenant.
